subject: Audit chain exportability, signed manifests & deletion attestations
messages:
From: Lydia Chang <lydia@finvero.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Cc: audit@finvero.com
Date: Mon, 13 Nov 2028 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Audit export — formats, signing and deletion attestations

Hi Karthik,

We're preparing for a regulatory inspection in Q1 and need to understand how Redwood can provide us with audit/access logs that meet two constraints:

1) We need an export that preserves event ordering and is verifiable (signed manifest or checksum per file).
2) We need a formal deletion attestation when we issue a cross-border erase request for tenant data (including logs).

Specifically: can you provide exports in NDJSON (newline-delimited JSON) with a signed manifest (SHA256) and a separate deletion-certificate document after erasure? Also: will exports for EU-hosted tenants be subject to any additional residency packaging (e.g. separate buckets per region)?

If helpful, we can share a short checklist of fields the regulator will expect. We'd like to map delivery options (S3/SFTP/API) to the attestation format and estimated lead times.

Thanks — Lydia
Lydia Chang
Head of Information Security, Finvero
lydia@finvero.com
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Lydia Chang <lydia@finvero.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 13 Nov 2028 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Audit export — formats, signing and deletion attestations

Hi Lydia — thanks for the clear ask. High-level answers up front: yes, we can deliver NDJSON with a signed manifest and provide a deletion attestation. Below I outline the modes and trade-offs; I'll include an example manifest and brief process in a follow-up message/attachment.

Delivery options we support (with pros/cons):
- SFTP bulk handoff (preferred for large historical pulls): we stream gzipped NDJSON files, produce a per-file SHA256 manifest plus an overall signed manifest (RSA-2048 signature historically; can support customer-wrapped keys). Typical handoff window: 24–72 hours for up to 3TB; expedite available.
- Object storage (customer S3/GCS/Azure): we stage files into a customer-controlled bucket in the requested cloud region; Redwood will publish the signed manifest to the same bucket. Good for continuous exports.
- API bulk export (cursored): paginated NDJSON pulled via authenticated API; each page includes a page_digest header (SHA256). Best for streaming consumers but not ideal for regulators expecting a single archive.

Residency packaging: for EU-hosted tenants we place exports into EU-only storage endpoints and provide a manifest that includes region tags per file. We do not mix blobs from different regions in the same export bundle unless explicitly requested.

Deletion attestation: we offer a certified deletion statement that includes:
- export bundle identifiers and SHA256 digests
- erasure timestamp (ISO 8601)
- operator ID who executed the erase
- deletion scope (logs, snapshots, KV cache)
- signed statement (PKCS#7) that can be sent to your compliance team

Open questions for us to size the work:
1) Expected export size and whether you prefer a one-time handoff vs continuous export.
2) Whether you'd like Redwood to wrap the manifest signature with a KMIP/HSM-managed key or use our platform key.
3) Any regulatory-specific fields beyond event timestamp, event_type, actor_id, resource_id, and tenant_id.

I'll attach an example manifest and a short readme with expected field names in my next message.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Senior Manager, Trust & Security — Redwood Inference
From: Lydia Chang <lydia@finvero.com>

Date: Tue, 14 Nov 2028 08:27:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Audit export — formats, signing and deletion attestations

Thanks Karthik — this is helpful. A couple follow-ups from our side:

• Size: initial export ~450GB (three months of audit logs). We'll likely do a one-time bulk handoff and then request weekly deltas (incremental NDJSON bundles).
• Signature: we'd prefer Redwood publish signatures that we can validate with your public cert; for deletion attestations we need an additional traceability field in the manifest linking bundle -> deletion-certificate id.
• Legal hold: for any active legal hold cases we need the ability to request a preservation hold that prevents deletion (and triggers a hold-specific manifest). How quickly can a preservation hold be applied and communicated?

Also, can you confirm the deletion workflow when we request an erasure for a tenant in the EU? We need the timeline, exactly what is removed (live data vs. backups vs. logs), and whether there is an option to receive a pre-deletion export for records retention before erasure.

Lydia
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Lydia Chang <lydia@finvero.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 15 Nov 2028 15:34:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Audit export — formats, signing and deletion attestations

Lydia — appreciate the extra detail. Below is a concrete plan and timeline proposal we can include in an SOC2 evidence packet if helpful.

Plan (one-time + weekly deltas):
- T+0 (one-time bulk): Redwood will generate gzipped NDJSON shards (max 50GB per shard) for the historic window and stage them on an EU-only SFTP endpoint you control. Each shard gets a companion .sha256 file. We also produce an overall manifest: manifest.json (includes file list, per-file digest, shard creation timestamp, operator id, tenant_id, region tag). The manifest is signed with Redwood's private key and we publish the corresponding public cert. We can optionally wrap the manifest signature with your KMS key via an HSM-based signing flow (requires a short integration/permission step).
- T+1 week (deltas): weekly delta bundles with the same format; each delta manifest references the previous manifest id to create an immutable chain.
- Preservation hold: can be enacted within 2 business hours for EU tenants by filing a preservation request through our support API (we require an authenticated request by a named Finvero admin). When placed, the preservation flag prevents automated deletion pipelines from removing logs and causes a hold-specific manifest to be generated.
- Deletion/erase: when you request erasure for a tenant we perform the following:
  * Suspend writes and snapshot live stores (immediate).
  * Issue pre-deletion export (if requested) within 24–48 hours and stage to your S3/SFTP.
  * Invoke erase jobs: wipe tenant live data; purge object blobs and mark tombstones for 3rd-party backup retention windows (we surface what we cannot immediately wipe, e.g., immutable cloud provider snapshots).
  * Post-erase attestation: we provide a signed deletion-certificate (PKCS#7) that lists erased items and SHA256 digests for bundles previously handed to you, plus operator id and timestamp. Where immediate wipe from provider snapshots is not possible, the attestation includes a remediation timeline and confirmation once cloud provider acknowledges snapshot deletion.

Next steps / ask from Finvero:
1) Confirm you want the HSM-wrapped signature option or Redwood-managed key.
2) Share the Finvero admin account email for the preservation API enactment.
3) Confirm SFTP host (we can provision a temporary staging server if you prefer).

Attachments: we have included an example manifest (audit_export_manifest_20281114.ndjson.sig) and a README that maps our event fields to the regulator checklist.

I'll loop in Ben for SLA/lead times and Marissa for delivery ops to coordinate the SFTP provisioning.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Senior Manager, Trust & Security — Redwood Inference
